title: Nelson and Others (Joined Cases C-581/10 and C-629/10), 23 October 2012
source: Nelson and Others (Joined Cases C-581/10 and C-629/10), 23 October 2012
excerpt: passengers whose flights are delayed are entitled to compensation under that regulation where they suffer, on account of such flights, a loss of time equal to or in excess of three hours, that is, where they reach their final destination three hours or more after the arrival time originally scheduled by the air carrier.
summary: The Grand Chamber confirmed Sturgeon: a delay of three hours or more at the final destination gives compensation.
